This is the OUTER diameter (OD); per Russian steel-pipe standards for trunk/branch gas pipelines (GOST 31447-2012 / GOST 20295-85, confirmed via a separate check of those standards), 530mm OD steel pipe is the standard product for nominal/conditional diameter Ду500 (DN500) -- i.e. this IS the sheet's 500mm nominal diameter, expressed in the OD convention rather than the DN convention, not a conflicting figure.

resolutions.researcher_notes: REFS_ADDED, replacing the prior ref (docviewer.yandex.com -- confirmed dead, same DiskNotFoundError finding as documented on the Length [ref] unit above; the whole underlying Yandex Disk document set for this project is gone). vologdaregion.ru states the pipe under construction as '530 мм' diameter, which on its face looks like a discrepancy against the sheet's 500mm. So the two figures describe the same pipe under different diameter conventions, not a material spec conflict. Recorded as a caveat in the paired validity record so this reasoning is visible to a human reviewer rather than silently resolved. resolutions.recommendation: No change to existence/classification/duplicate status. P1456 is a real, well-documented 1959-commissioned Soviet-era trunk gas pipeline (803 km, 720mm, Serpukhov [Moscow Oblast] to Leningrad/Saint Petersburg via Kalinin/Tver oblast), independently confirmed by a third-party industrial database (energybase.ru), Gazprom's own subsidiary's 50th-anniversary press release (gazprom.ru via Wayback, since the live host connect-times-out from this machine), and two independent Russian trade/regional-press retrospectives (bloknot-stavropol.ru 2025, neftianka.ru). Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are both directly and consistently stated. Not a duplicate of, or misclassification against, any other row in this 28-PID roster: it is clearly distinct from the later, geographically separate Gryazovets-Leningrad pipeline family (P5534/P5535) and the Gryazovets-Vyborg lines (P0746/P5585), which run a different, more northerly corridor sourced from Vologda-region gas rather than Stavropol gas relayed via the Moscow-area Serpukhov-Moscow trunk; and distinct from Belousovo-Leningrad, a separate 1967-built pipeline that shares reconstruction contractors and combined funding with P1456 in several sources but is NOT itself a PID in this roster (no cross_row_lead needed). CAVEAT 1 (operator): Gazprom's own 2009 primary source names TWO joint operators for this line -- Gazprom Transgaz Saint Petersburg AND Gazprom Transgaz Moscow -- consistent with the line crossing both companies' territorial zones; only Transgaz Saint Petersburg is staged as the single Operator value (see Operator [ref] researcher_notes) since it is also the entity named in a live, current (2026) maintenance tender. CAVEAT 2 (cost): the only cost figure found (~40 billion rubles, neftegaz.ru 2016) is an aggregate covering a COMBINED reconstruction program spanning both Serpukhov-Leningrad and the separate, non-roster Belousovo-Leningrad pipeline -- correctly left UNRESOLVED for SegmentCost rather than misattributed to this row alone. CAVEAT 3 (pressure): a 5.4 MPa figure appearing in 2020 reconstruction-approval press coverage is explicitly scoped to a small NEW branch spur (150mm, 3.6km, connecting a Novgorod CHP plant) built as part of the 9th reconstruction stage, not the 720mm main trunk's own rated pressure -- correctly left UNRESOLVED rather than misattributed.

resolutions.recommendation: P2312 (Gryazovets-KGMO / "Grязовец-КГМО", also referenced as "KGMO-2") is a real, existing, correctly-classified operating trunk transmission gas pipeline. Existence and classification are independently confirmed by energybase.ru (third-party infrastructure database; explicit 'магистральный газопровод' / trunk pipeline language in its own 2026 procurement-notice text, status 'в эксплуатации'/operating), Gazprom Transgaz Moscow's own June-2018 press release (names it explicitly as 'КГМО-2 (Грязовец-КГМО, 498 км)' feeding KRP-14), and a 2023 Gazprom Transgaz Moscow anniversary article for its Kryukovskoye LPUMG branch (lists 'Грязовец-КГМО' by name among the trunk lines that branch maintains). No duplicate/relabel risk found against this batch's 28-pipeline NW roster: gem.wiki's own 'Associated infrastructure' framing and this batch's brief both correctly treat P2312 as the Gryazovets FEED line INTO the separate KGMO ring system, not a duplicate of the ring itself or of any sibling roster row. CAVEATS (all spec-level, none existence/classification/duplicate-level): (1) LENGTH -- sheet's 498.00 km is exactly matched by the Gazprom Transgaz Moscow primary source, but energybase.ru states a conflicting 458 km for the same named pipeline; recommend keeping 498 km (matches the operator's own source and the existing sheet value) but flagging the 40km discrepancy. (2) DIAMETER -- sheet's 1200mm could not be independently verified this pass (GEM's own wiki citation for this value, seltim.ru, is a confirmed dead link/404); energybase.ru states a conflicting 1220mm for the same pipeline. Left UNRESOLVED rather than picking a side. (3) CAPACITY SCOPE MISMATCH -- gem.wiki's own 'Capacity: 90 bcm/y (projected)' figure is, on inspection of gem.wiki's own Background-section context, a SYSTEM-LEVEL projected capacity for the KGMO ring's Noginsk-Voskresensk segment (traceable to a Ministry of Energy planning-list document), not a Gryazovets-KGMO-specific figure -- this is exactly the kind of aggregate-vs-segment misattribution this batch's brief warned about, and it was caught and NOT staged as this row's Capacity. (4) LOCATION -- StartPrefecture/District='Gryazovetsky District' is only a geographic inference (no source names the district verbatim, though the Gryazovets compressor station's location in the town of Gryazovets makes it a very safe inference); EndPrefecture/District='Dmitrovsky District' as currently recorded on the sheet could NOT be verified -- gem.wiki attributes it to energybase.ru, but energybase.ru's live page (exhaustively searched) contains zero occurrences of 'Дмитров' anywhere. The only supporting signal found is that Kryukovskoye LPUMG, which does maintain this exact pipeline, also operates a compressor station in Yakhroma (a Dmitrovsky District town) -- circumstantial, not a direct statement that THIS pipeline terminates in that district specifically (Kryukovskoye LPUMG's service area spans multiple Moscow Oblast districts). Flagging EndPrefecture/District as an unresolved attribution claim for a future pass rather than either removing it or treating it as confirmed.

resolutions.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: real, independently confirmed. A Russian Ministry of Energy public-servitude notice (mosertolovo.ru, a municipal government site hosting the federal notice) names this exact federal linear object ('...газопровода Ленинград-Выборг-Госграница... в составе стройки «КС «Северная» (газопровод Ленинград-Выборг-Госграница)') and lists dozens of cadastral parcels along its route through Vsevolozhsky then Vyborgsky District. A Gazprom Transgaz Saint Petersburg subsidiary page (spb-tr.gazprom.ru, via Wayback) and an engineering contractor's project list (proektneftegaz.ru) independently corroborate the line's identity and ongoing maintenance/reconstruction activity through 2021. This is not a GEM-only or single-source entity.
CLASSIFICATION: correctly classified transmission gas pipeline (магистральный газопровод) -- confirmed by Gazprom's own subsidiary page language and energybase.ru's 'all Gazprom PJSC trunk pipelines' grouping.
DUPLICATE CHECK: NOT a duplicate of P5590 (Leningrad-Vyborg-State Border II). The servitude PDF separately names 'Ленинград – Выборг – Госграница-2' as a distinct linear object in one parcel entry; proektneftegaz.ru separately lists reconstruction work scoped to '...Госграница-1' specifically (distinct from the joint '-1,2' references); spb-tr.gazprom.ru groups both under one branch's zone of responsibility as '-- 1, 2' (two named strings, not one). Identical LengthKnown/Diameter/Capacity on P2335 and P5590 is explained by both being genuine parallel строки (nitki) of the same corridor built to the same spec, not a copy-paste error -- consistent with how this batch's other twin-string pairs (Gryazovets-Vyborg I/II, Gryazovets-Leningrad I/II) are modeled.
ATTRIBUTION: Owner (Gazprom PJSC 100%) and Operator (Gazprom Transgaz Saint Petersburg) both independently corroborated -- see fills[].
SPEC CAVEAT (the one open item): ru.wikipedia's 'Выборг — Иматра' history article states the original 1973-74 Leningrad-Karelian Isthmus-to-Finnish-border joint pipeline was built of 800mm pipe over a 160km route with 6 bcm/y capacity, opened with a Finnish-Soviet ceremony 9 Jan 1974 -- materially different from GEM's currently recorded 1220mm diameter, 115km length, and 9.13 bcm/y capacity. However, a genuinely independent, current, non-GEM technical database (energybase.ru) states exactly GEM's current figures (1220mm/115km/9.13 bcm/y), and documented ongoing reconstruction work (crane replacement, pressure-reduction-point reconstruction, КС Северная 2nd-stage compressor-station work) makes a diameter uprate and/or route realignment over 50+ years entirely plausible; the 160km history figure may also simply include the ~40-50km Finnish-territory stretch to Imatra/Valkeala that is out of scope for this Russia-only GEM row (which runs only to the state border). I could not find a document dating a specific reconstruction/uprate event, so I am NOT proposing a value change -- but flagging this so a future pass knows both figures exist in the record and why I left the current ones standing.

resolutions.recommendation: P3176 is a real, substantially/fully built 880km trunk gas pipeline running from Gryazovets, Gryazovetsky District, Vologda Oblast, to KS Slavyanskaya, Kingisepp District, Leningrad Oblast (the Nord Stream 2 head compressor station). It is officially item 9 of Приложение N4 to Russian government decree No. 816-r ('Развитие газотранспортных мощностей ЕСГ Северо-Западного региона, участок Грязовец - КС Славянская', sudact.ru consolidated text read), and is the subject of at least 10 independent primary/trade-press documents describing its construction (2018-2022), contractors (Stroygazmontazh as GC; Gazregion, Lengazspetsstroy, Krasnodargazstroy, Neftegazkomplektmontazh, SPKh Nauka as subcontractors), investor/owner (Gazprom PJSC via Gazprom Invest LLC), and operating subsidiaries (Gazprom Transgaz Ukhta for the Vologda Oblast segment, Gazprom Transgaz Saint Petersburg for the Leningrad Oblast segment/terminus). NOT a duplicate: distinct from the parallel Gryazovets-Vyborg corridor (P0746/P5585, a separate, older, 917km/1400mm pipeline built earlier to feed the original Nord Stream), from Gryazovets-Leningrad (P5534/P5535), and from the Ukhta-Torzhok variants (P1439 etc.) -- this is the newer corridor built specifically circa 2017-2022 to feed Nord Stream 2's head station while also serving NW/Central Russia gasification and the Ust-Luga industrial zone (confirmed by the RIA/Neftegaz/decree capacity-increase reporting explicitly naming both purposes). Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are directly and repeatedly confirmed ('МГП' = магистральный газопровод in nearly every source). CAVEAT (not a disqualifying concern, but material -- see status_reviews[] for the full discussion): the newest dated primary evidence of construction/commissioning activity found in this research pass is Dec-2022 (compressor-shop commissioning); no source dated 2023-2026 was found that explicitly confirms the trunk is presently transporting gas. GEM's own wiki text itself hedges 'As of July 2023 ... presumed to be operating' rather than stating it as confirmed fact. This is flagged as a caveat on the Status verdict, not an existence/classification/duplicate problem with the row itself.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Existence and identity confirmed independently of GEM: a Russian federal government territorial-planning decree (sudact.ru, item 31 of the trunk-gas-pipeline schedule under Government Order 816-r) names this exact project and route; independent regional press (newsvo.ru 2016, vologda.mk.ru + vologdaregion.ru 2020, TASS via Wayback 2016) and a primary operator source (mrg.gazprom.ru, Gazprom's Vologda gas-distribution subsidiary, via Wayback) all corroborate the same project under the same name/route across a 2016-2022 span. Status=operating for Stage I specifically is independently confirmed by the mrg.gazprom.ru source, which states gas reached Kirillovsky District (this stage's terminus) by end of 2021. TWO CAVEATS surfaced during this sweep and recorded separately: (1) a Diameter unit discrepancy (530mm vs the sheet's 500mm) resolved as a units-convention non-issue -- 530mm is the standard OUTER diameter for Ду500/DN500 nominal pipe under GOST 31447-2012/20295-85, not a different pipe; (2) a genuine SegmentCost concern -- the only source giving the exact 22,000,000,000 RUB figure on the sheet states it explicitly as the FOUR-STAGE PROJECT TOTAL, not a Stage-I-specific cost (see the separate 'concern' validity record, contested=SegmentCost). Also note: this project's own primary/operator sources (mrg.gazprom.ru, vologdaregion.ru) describe capacity and route figures at the whole-project (all 4 stages / 412 km) level far more often than at the per-stage level GEM records; the Capacity fill on this row applies the whole-project 743 million m3/y figure to Stage I under a reasoned uniform-diameter/constant-capacity exception, flagged there and here for a human reviewer's judgment rather than silently applied.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The only source found stating the exact 22,000,000,000 RUB figure that matches the sheet's SegmentCost is vologdaregion.ru (11-Feb-2020), which is explicit and unambiguous that this is the TOTAL investment for constructing all FOUR stages of the project combined: 'Общий объем инвестиций для реализации четырех этапов строительства составит 22 млрд рублей' (total investment for implementation of the four stages of construction will be 22 billion rubles). resolutions.recommendation: Minor, informational naming tension -- not recommended for any sheet edit, documented so a future pass does not re-discover it as new. THREE sources give three different labels for what appears to be the same 1981-commissioned Ukhta-Gryazovets line: (1) OSM relation 17195756 (the source GEM's own routes repo draws from) names it 'Пунга — Ухта — Грязовец 4' (segment/stage 4 = GEM's 'IV', matching this row's segment_name and OtherLanguagePrimaryPipelineName); (2) siyanie-severa.ru's historical account calls the 1981-commissioned 4th stage of the wider 'Север-Центр' system 'Уренгой — Ухта — Грязовец' (Urengoy-Ukhta-Gryazovets), with the corridor's 3rd stage (Dec 1977) called 'Пунга — Ухта — Торжок' (Punga-Ukhta-Torzhok); (3) Gazprom Transgaz Ukhta's own 2023 company-newspaper history timeline places, under the year 1981, the commissioning of 'Пунга – Ухта – Грязовец III' -- i.e. the OPERATING COMPANY's own archive calls the 1981 line 'III', not 'IV'. All three sources agree on the 1981 date and the physical Ukhta-Gryazovets routing; they disagree only on the ordinal label and which upstream city (Punga vs Urengoy) to prefix. This is very plausibly just inconsistent popular/company usage of an internal Soviet 'queue' numbering system across nearly 50 years of sources, not evidence of a different physical pipeline -- but it is close enough to the kind of confusion that produces real duplicate-PID errors elsewhere in this roster that it is worth a second researcher's eyes. resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed real via multiple documents (Gazprom Transgaz Ukhta's own Urdomskoye LPUMG page and 2017 anniversary newspaper, Gazprom Invest's encyclopedia page, ru.wikipedia's 'Сияние Севера' article, and a 2025 regional-press article on a modernization/dismantling plan for its sibling strings) -- not a GEM-only or hallucinated entity. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a natural-gas trunk/transmission pipeline (fuel=Gas, type=transmission); no evidence of NGL or gathering/feeder misclassification. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of any other row in this batch -- P5541 (String I, 1969, 1220mm), P5542 (String II, 1975, 1220mm) and P5543 (String III, 1977-78, 1420mm) are three genuinely distinct physical pipe strings built in sequence, confirmed via a single primary source (Urdomskoye LPUMG page) that lists all three with distinct years/diameters in one passage. THE ACTUAL FINDING: this batch's real risk is a SOURCING/DISAMBIGUATION hazard, not a wrong value. Russia's gas-transport network has TWO different 'Ukhta-Torzhok' systems that share nearly identical Russian names and even the same Gazprom-family URL pattern: (1) the OLD Vuktyl-era system built 1969-1978 as three parallel 'nitki' (strings) -- P5541/P5542/P5543, this row's family; and (2) a NEW, much later Yamal-era system built 2012-2017 in two stages, both 1420mm/9.8 MPa/45 bcm/y -- corresponding to GEM rows P0767 and P1439. The CURRENT_REF already on file for P5543's Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Location (proektirovanie.gazprom.ru/.../ukhta-torzhok/) is PRIMARILY a project page about the NEW system's Stage II (i.e. it is actually P1439's correct dedicated primary source, not P5543's). On close reading, that page does contain one passing but explicit and useful sentence naming the OLD trio by number ('Ухта — Торжок (I, II, III нитки)') as existing, currently-operating parallel infrastructure in the same corridor -- so it is not actively WRONG as a supporting reference for this row, and no data value here needs to change. But a future researcher skimming only the page title/topic could easily paste this same URL onto P0767/P1439's Status/Location cells thinking it is redundant, or could mistake P5543's own StartYear/Diameter for the Yamal system's, given both are named 'Ukhta-Torzhok' with Roman-numeral stage/string labels. Verdict is 'confirmed (caveat)' rather than 'concern' because no recorded value on this row is actually wrong -- the caveat is purely a documentation/disambiguation note for whoever next touches P5541, P5542, P0767, or P1439.

Confirmed via one independent Russian oil/gas trade-press source (nangs.org, 2021 major-overhaul completion article) plus multiple Gazprom-family documents (Gazprom Dobycha Krasnodar's own ЛПУМТ branch org-history page, a Jan-2020 Gazprom Dobycha Krasnodar press release specifically about this pipeline, and Gazprom Transgaz Ukhta's 2017 house-journal historical retrospective). TWO SPELLING/TYPO CORRECTIONS made per batch guidance, both same-entity standardizations, not factual disputes: (1) Operator 'Gazprom Dobycha Karsnodar LLC' -> 'Gazprom Dobycha Krasnodar LLC' (typo); (2) StartState/Province 'Republic of Komi' -> 'Komi Republic' (canonical GEM spelling, matching EndState/Province already on this row). The seemingly odd geography (a Komi-region pipeline operated by a company named for Krasnodar, ~2,500km away) is a GENUINE, well-documented administrative fact (an Oct-2014 restructuring folded the Komi-region operating branch into Gazprom Dobycha Krasnodar, which operates assets across 8 Russian regions per its own repeated corporate boilerplate) and is NOT a misattribution or copy-paste error -- confirmed across three separately-read documents. Separately, this row's routes-repo geojson contains a geometry-contamination defect (a fragment belonging to the different Пунга-Вуктыл-Ухта system) -- see the companion validity[] 'route' concern record; this does not affect the sheet's own recorded StartState/Province/EndState/Province values, both of which are correctly Komi Republic only.
